| Institution | IPEDS‑reported “Cost I” (2023‑24) – Total Cost of Attendance (full‑time, first‑time, degree/certificate‑seeking undergraduates, in‑state, on campus) |
|-------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

**Why University of Wyoming wins**

* The IPEDS “Cost I” data report the most complete and comparable picture of the total cost of attendance, including tuition & fees, on‑campus housing & food, books & supplies, and other on‑campus expenses.

Using the IPEDS “total cost of attendance” (Cost I) for in‑state, on‑campus, full‑time, first‑time degree/certificate‑seeking undergraduate students, **the University of Wyoming has the highest cost for the 2023‑24 academic year in the least‑populated U.S. state (Wyoming), excluding Wyoming Tech**.

# University of Wyoming Tuition & Financial Aid
University of Wyoming's tuition is $8,530 for in-state and $25,390 for out-of-state students. Compared with the national average cost of in-state tuition of $12,808, University of Wyoming is cheaper. For students coming from out of state, the tuition is cheaper than the national average cost of out-of-state tuition of $30,702.
These figures include both tuition and fees, also referred to as the sticker price. Fees differ by institution and may fund library services, student gym facilities, student centers, technology resources and campus health centers.
As you’re comparing costs of different institutions, also consider the total cost and the net price. The total cost is the tuition and fees, plus the cost of food and housing, books and supplies, and transportation and personal expenses. At University of Wyoming, the total cost is $27,205 for in-state students and $43,825 for out-of-state students. The net price is the average cost of the university after aid and scholarship funds are discounted from the total cost, which come in on average at $19,283 for in-state students and $37,961 for out-of-state students receiving need-based aid.

# University of Wyoming Tuition & Financial Aid
University of Wyoming's tuition is $8,530 for in-state and $25,390 for out-of-state students. Compared with the national average cost of in-state tuition of $12,808, University of Wyoming is cheaper. For students coming from out of state, the tuition is cheaper than the national average cost of out-of-state tuition of $30,702.
These figures include both tuition and fees, also referred to as the sticker price. Fees differ by institution and may fund library services, student gym facilities, student centers, technology resources and campus health centers.
As you’re comparing costs of different institutions, also consider the total cost and the net price. The total cost is the tuition and fees, plus the cost of food and housing, books and supplies, and transportation and personal expenses. At University of Wyoming, the total cost is $27,205 for in-state students and $43,825 for out-of-state students. The net price is the average cost of the university after aid and scholarship funds are discounted from the total cost, which come in on average at $19,283 for in-state students and $37,961 for out-of-state students receiving need-based aid.

Understanding costs and financial aid at Casper College Foundation, tied closely to Casper College's open admissions policy, is key for students and parents planning ahead. | Institution | IPEDS‑reported “Cost I” (2023‑24) – Total Cost of Attendance (full‑time, first‑time, degree/certificate‑seeking undergraduates, in‑state, on campus) |
|-------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| University of Wyoming | **≈ $35,008** – Tuition $6,938 + housing & food $17,260 + books & supplies $1,670 + other on‑campus expenses $9,140【6†source】 |

| Casper College | ≈ $15,000 – (IPED‑reported “published cost of attendance” for in‑state, on‑campus full‑time, first‑time undergraduates)【7†source】 |

**Why University of Wyoming wins**

* The IPEDS “Cost I” data report the most complete and comparable picture of the total cost of attendance, including tuition & fees, on‑campus housing & food, books & supplies, and other on‑campus expenses.
* Washington State’s only public four‑year institution, U. Wyoming has the highest figure of **$35,008** for the 2023‑24 academic year, which is higher than all other Wyoming institutions (Central Wyoming, Laramie County, Casper, and the excluded WY Tech).

Using the IPEDS “total cost of attendance” (Cost I) for in‑state, on‑campus, full‑time, first‑time degree/certificate‑seeking undergraduate students, **the University of Wyoming has the highest cost for the 2023‑24 academic year in the least‑populated U.S. state (Wyoming), excluding Wyoming Tech**.
